title: Efficient Approximate Decomposition Solver using Ising Model
problem: Finding approximate Boolean decompositions with minimal error is computationally expensive, limiting practical deployment of energy-efficient lookup table (LUT) based computing with memory. Traditional solvers require long computation times to discover decompositions that reduce LUT size while maintaining acceptable accuracy.
motivation: Approximate computing with memory (LUT-based implementation) is energy-efficient, but the decomposition search process must be accelerated to make this approach practical.
method: Reformulates approximate Boolean decomposition as an Ising model optimization problem to leverage quantum-inspired solvers. Proposes a column-based approximate disjoint decomposition method that fits the Ising model formulation. Adapts the problem to Ising model-based solvers and introduces two improvement techniques for efficient search when using simulated bifurcation to solve the underlying Ising model.
key_novelty: Reformulating approximate Boolean decomposition as an Ising optimization problem enables the use of quantum-inspired solvers like simulated bifurcation, achieving both faster convergence and lower error than traditional approaches.
contributions: Column-based approximate disjoint decomposition method compatible with Ising model formulation
Adaptation of Boolean decomposition problem to Ising model-based optimization solvers
Two improvement techniques for efficient simulated bifurcation search
Achieves 11% smaller mean error distance with 1.16× speedup over state-of-the-art
limitations: Scalability to larger Boolean functions beyond 16-input and applicability to real-world workloads not discussed.
primary_theme: Ising model-based Boolean function decomposition optimization
